subject: Re: RTBF / deletion workflow — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Privacy Ops <privacy-ops@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: RTBF / deletion workflow — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Alex / Privacy team —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of ask:
- FintechCo needs a documented Right to Be Forgotten (RTBF) workflow for customer delete requests that covers: immediate removal from active serving, purge from backups, retention of audit logs for compliance, and enforcement across EU data residency zones.

What we covered on the call:
- Hot storage & model inputs: we can delete PII and user payloads from active databases and object stores within 48 hours after a validated request.
- Cache & KV: session/KV caches are purged on delete requests; KV entries are segregated per-customer where configured.
- Logs & telemetry: application logs are retained for X days by default; we can scope logs to exclude PII and provide filtered exports for audits.
- Backups: snapshot retention is typically 90 days; full irreversible purge from immutable backups requires coordination and is often delayed by legal holds.
- Data residency: if you pin a region we will run deletion flows in that region and confirm cross-region copies are accounted for.

Agreed next steps:
1) I’ll send a written RTBF workflow with timelines and any constraints (backups, legal hold scenarios) — attached. (Action: Camila)
2) FintechCo to confirm whether legal holds or audit requirements might prevent immediate backup purge. (Action: Alex / Privacy Ops)
3) If acceptable, we’ll include a 90-day backup purge target with exceptions captured in the MOU; we’ll also provide a signed attestation when purge completes. (Action: Camila + Redwood Ops)

Attachments: RTBF_workflow_v1.pdf (workflow + timelines), backup-retention-table.csv (existing snapshot lifecycle by class)

If anything above is incorrect or missing, let me know and I’ll update the doc. Otherwise I’ll get the workflow updated and loop in our infra team.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Thanks Camila — appreciate the clear recap. A couple of clarifications before you finalize the doc: 

1) Backups: when you say 90 days for purge, do you mean complete irreversible deletion from cold snapshots (we use encrypted S3 glacier-like tiers)? We need the timeline and any manual steps called out.
2) Logs: we have a compliance requirement to keep certain audit trails for 2 years, but we can mask PII. Can you outline how you’d provide an audited attestation that PII was removed while preserving audit metadata?
3) Data residency: we have EU customers for whom data must not leave eu-west-1. Can you confirm where Redwood stores any intermediate artifacts during deletion (e.g., job queues, temp storage)?

Also, can you provide the contact for the infra lead who will actually run the purge and confirm completion?

Alex

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RTBF / deletion workflow — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Alex —

Great questions — answers below and I’ve updated the attached RTBF_workflow_v1.pdf to reflect these points. Summary bullets first, details after.

Summary answers:
- Backups: 90-day target for purge from snapshot-based backups. For encrypted cold storage (Glacier), we treat purge as a multi-step process: identify snapshots containing the customer namespace -> schedule deletion -> verify bytes removed and provide cryptographic checksum confirmation. If there is a legal hold, we will flag and exclude those snapshots until hold is resolved.
- Logs: We will provide an attestation describing the steps taken: PII redaction (deterministic hashing or removal), retention windows for audit metadata, and an export of non-PII audit records. The export will include event timestamps, actor IDs, and redaction markers.
- Data residency: All deletion jobs for EU-pinned customers run within eu-west-1; intermediate work queues and temporary storage are provisioned in-region. Cross-region backups are flagged and included in the purge plan; we will not copy artifacts across regions as part of deletion.
- Infra contact: Dylan Brooks (dylan.brooks@redwood.ai) will own the execution and verification of purge runs; he’s CC’d here.

Detailed notes:
1) Hot delete (0–48 hrs): validated delete request -> remove user records from primary DBs and object stores; update indexes and caches; send confirmation to requestor.
2) KV/Cache (0–48 hrs): purge per-customer cache partitions; session tokens invalidated.
3) Logs (configurable): by default we retain application logs 180 days; we can configure per-account retention. PII is redacted before storage; where regulations require audit trace, redacted audit views are provided.
4) Backups (0–90 days): snapshot retention policies depend on class (daily/weekly/monthly). We will:
   - identify snapshots containing the customer namespace
   - schedule deletion windows (can be batched)
   - provide proof-of-deletion artifacts (S3 metadata + checksum)
   - notify FintechCo and include the attestation in the hubspot deal record

Constraints / exceptions:
- Legal hold or active investigations will delay irreversible deletion; in that case we can provide a documented exception and timeline.
- Immutable backups managed by third-party partners may have additional constraints; we’ll surface those per-case.

Next steps (revised):
- I’ll schedule a short (15–20 min) sync with Dylan and your infra/privacy ops to walk the purge playbook and finalize timelines. (Action: Camila)
- Dylan will provide a sample proof-of-deletion artifact for your security team. (Action: Dylan)

I’ve attached the updated RTBF_workflow_v1.pdf and the backup-retention-table.csv. Let me know your availability for a quick sync tomorrow.

Best,
Camila
